summary: Overnight credits double-counted during large batch inference run
description: Customer reports an unexpected spike in credit consumption after an automated overnight batch of embeddings + generation. BrightCart states they had a single scheduled job hitting a pinned model variant but billing shows ~2x expected credits and metering logs indicate requests were attributed to two model variants and multiple retries. Customer requests: 1) explanation of root cause 2) credit adjustment for the excess usage 3) mitigation to prevent recurrence.
impact: Customer incurred approximately 2.3x their expected credit consumption for the billing day (estimated extra ~18k credits). This affects BrightCart's monthly committed usage and could trigger overage notifications. Job traffic relates to production recommender and is customer-facing (ecommerce recommender latency-sensitive).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer scheduled nightly batch (cron job) at 02:15 UTC to generate 1M embeddings + context generations against pinned model gptx-v2-13b.
2) Job uses Redwood hosted API with project key scoped to dedicated pool.
3) Observe metering logs and billing for the date 2026-03-05.
4) Customer reports double-counted credits compared to local estimate.

Metering aggregated shows two entries for same request_id across primary/fallback with full cost allocation each.
investigation_notes: 03/06 10:00 Support: Initial triage with BrightCart, obtained job schedule, sample request_ids and invoice snapshot.
03/06 13:20 SRE: Confirmed duplicate attribution pattern in metering where fallback routing entries were charged in full alongside primary entries for same request_id.

03/06 15:45 Eng (serving-runtime): Hypothesis - autoscaler triggered model variant fallback during short spike; retry logic produced a successful response on fallback while primary also completed, and metering deduplication did not collapse duplicates because dedupe key was not propagated across routing handoffs.
03/07 09:10 Billing: Calculated provisional excess ~18,400 credits on 2026-03-05 for BrightCart account.
03/07 11:30 Eng: Identified related code path in routing middleware where request_uuid header was regenerated on failover; tracing shows two separate meter events with different dedupe keys.
03/07 16:00 Patch proposal created to ensure original request_uuid is preserved across fallback and retries (see PR).

support_actions: Requested signed CSV export of the customer's job IDs and invoice snapshot (provided by customer 03/07 18:15).
Created reproducible test harness in staging to simulate autoscaler-induced fallback with high concurrency (PR created).
Billing calculated provisional excess and applied a temporary credit hold pending root cause verification.
Eng scheduled hotfix to preserve request_uuid across routing handoffs; sequencing ensures no behavioral change to existing retries other than dedupe key propagation.
resolution: Work in progress: A code fix to preserve the original request UUID across fallback and retry paths has been implemented in PR #9876 and deployed to staging. Once validated in staging, we'll roll the fix to prod during a low-traffic window and reconcile billing. Billing has provisionally applied a credit hold equal to the estimated excess (18,400 credits) pending final verification.

Document mitigation steps in internal runbook and notify dedicated customers of potential transient double-charge scenarios (owner: Support, due: 2026-03-15).
